_comment: The wildlife as individuals (scripts/sim/wildlife.gd): every land animal and bird has a home and goes about its life there, drawn top-down at its size in the world (exaggerated so it reads, like the ships). land: for each land animal (data/birds.json land_animals has their names, groups and facts): km (its length in the world), home (what it lives in, drawn on the map: rookery, snow_den, cave, den, burrow, tree, tree_nest, leaf_nest, waterhole, wallow, pride_rock; none for one that just roams), active (day, night or dusk: when it's up and about; otherwise it's at its home, or bedded down where it is), groups (how many groups live round each of the map's spots for it), spread_km (how far round the spot), roam_km (how far from its home a group ranges), kmh (its walking speed), hibernate (months a whole group sleeps in its den), den_young (a mother with young keeps to the den in hibernate months), migrate ({months: when it's away, to: [lon, lat] degrees from its home}: the herd walks there over migrate_days at the start of them, and back at the end). birds: each class's home (where its birds roost and nest: a gull colony on the shore near its port, a raptor's eyrie, a cormorant colony, a heronry, a seabird colony), species homes for the ones that differ (bitterns in the reeds, cranes on the ground), each class's numbers at a port (gulls by the port's size band; the others as birds.json's own [chance, fewest, most]), how far (km) seabirds range from their colony to forage and follow ships, and how far gulls follow ships out from port. Birds whose range only covers a port some months spend the rest at the nearest port it covers then, flying between them over migrate_days at the start of each stay. km: birds' and homes' sizes in the world.
